input: Host a board game tournament for neighbors

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of participants and how many games are played determines the bracket structure, space needed, and how long the event runs.
Knowing the age range and mix of guests (families with kids, adults only, mixed) affects game selection, rules complexity, and overall tone.
The venue (indoors at home, backyard, community space) and the date/time directly shape logistics like seating, lighting, and scheduling.
The available budget determines whether food, prizes, printed brackets, and decorations are feasible.
Knowing which specific board game(s) will be played is the single most important factor in designing the tournament format and rules.
The desired vibe — casual and social vs. competitive and structured — shapes how strictly rules are enforced, whether prizes matter, and how the event is communicated.
Understanding what a great outcome looks like (everyone had fun, a clear winner crowned, neighbors feel more connected) helps prioritise trade-offs throughout planning.

gold.taskTitle: Host a board game tournament for neighbors
gold.taskDescription: Plan and run a board game tournament event for neighbors in the local community.

questions.title: How many neighbors do you expect to participate?
questions.description: The headcount determines the bracket format (single elimination, round robin, etc.), the amount of space needed, and how long the event will run.

questions.title: What is the age range of the guests attending?
questions.description: Knowing whether it is adults only, families with young children, or a mixed crowd directly affects which games are appropriate and how complex the rules can be.

questions.title: Where and when are you planning to hold this?
questions.description: The venue (your home, backyard, community hall) and the date and time shape seating arrangements, lighting, noise limits, and the overall schedule.

questions.title: What is your budget for the event?
questions.description: The budget determines what is feasible for prizes, food and drinks, printed materials like brackets or scorecards, and any decorations.

questions.title: Which board game or games will the tournament feature?
questions.description: The specific game chosen is the single biggest factor in designing the tournament format, round length, and scoring rules.

questions.title: Should the atmosphere be casual and social or seriously competitive?
questions.description: The desired vibe influences how strictly rules are enforced, whether prizes are a central focus, and how the event is promoted to neighbors.

questions.title: What does a successful tournament look like to you?
questions.description: Clarifying the primary goal — crowning a clear winner, building community bonds, or simply having fun — helps prioritise every planning decision.
